bug_semantics: Untrusted Python plugin source is parsed and passed through DangerousPatternVisitor before PluginManager imports it, but the visitor introduced in the BIC only rejects enumerated calls, modules, and narrow builtins access. It does not reject dangerous ast.Attribute traversal such as __bases__, __subclasses__, __globals__, __code__, and __mro__. A plugin can therefore produce no critical AST violation, be accepted even in the default strict mode, traverse Python's object hierarchy to recover a function's globals/builtins, and invoke system-command functionality outside the intended sandbox.
flaw_origin: Commit 50bec5d3656d62b8dbbb0ce082fd67b8436677fd created openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_ast_analyzer.py and wired analyze_plugin_code() into PluginManager._validate_plugin_file(). Its new DangerousPatternVisitor.visit_Call() and visit_Attribute() recognized specific dangerous names but had no dangerous-dunder set or general dunder-attribute check, thereby first writing the advisory's flawed AST-validation mechanism.
ai_marker: The exact BIC commit object identifies human author and committer Tobi <jahlives@gmx.ch> and contains both exact AI markers: "🤖 Generated with Claude Code" and "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>".
evidence: The repository-published advisory at https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-w7gr-9g4g-33mx and its first-party API record at https://api.github.com/repos/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security-advisories/GHSA-w7gr-9g4g-33mx name openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_ast_analyzer.py:41-316, describe the __class__/__bases__/__subclasses__()/__globals__/__code__/__mro__ traversal, show a chain reaching ['system']('whoami'), state impact as plugin code passing AST validation and escaping at runtime, declare the package range < 1.4.0, and identify resolution commit 993cd13 on feature/v1.4.x-development.

`git log --all --reverse -S'DangerousPatternVisitor' -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_ast_analyzer.py` returns exactly one first writer: 50bec5d3656d62b8dbbb0ce082fd67b8436677fd, parent cdc9c7d814915a9a2c568987b7bcc14f3b7cf533. `git log --follow` likewise starts this file at that commit. The commit is a normal one-parent commit, not a merge, move, revert, backport, or squash needing decomposition.

The BIC diff at https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/50bec5d3656d62b8dbbb0ce082fd67b8436677fd creates the 325-line analyzer and integrates it in openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_manager.py. At that tree, PluginManager(strict_security_mode=True) calls _validate_plugin_file() before load_plugin() imports the module; analyze_plugin_code() returns safe when the visitor reports no critical violation. visit_Attribute() only checks direct __builtins__/builtins access and visit_Call() only handles enumerated calls/getattr patterns, so the advisory's dunder traversal is accepted.

Direct-parent tree verification used `git cat-file -e cdc9c7d814915a9a2c568987b7bcc14f3b7cf533:openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_ast_analyzer.py`; Git returned `path ... does not exist`, proving the complete vulnerable analyzer file and its vulnerable lines are absent from the BIC's immediate parent. The BIC diff's new-file mode 100644 from /dev/null independently confirms that absence.

The direct fix at https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/993cd13d581a15821cb170df14627af1f1c1b1c3 adds DANGEROUS_DUNDER_ATTRIBUTES containing __mro__, __subclasses__, __bases__, __globals__, __builtins__, __code__, __reduce__, and __reduce_ex__; rejects direct dangerous-dunder ast.Attribute nodes; rejects __subclasses__() calls; and rejects constant dangerous dunder names supplied to getattr(). Its message explicitly resolves GHSA-w7gr-9g4g-33mx.

Version ancestry resolves v1.3.6 to f69305effbab0bdc0c8df0f2297cdfddf8929b6e and v1.4.0 to 768df5cd1910e349509f07a27eeac6951e0003bf. `git for-each-ref --contains` shows neither the BIC nor fix in any tag before v1.4.0, and shows both in v1.4.0 and every later v1.4 tag. `git merge-base` returns 0f0ffc0c8d9bba6d8a03e4721920fb5aad8a313a for BIC versus v1.3.6 (so v1.3.6 lacks this AST implementation), but returns the BIC itself for BIC versus v1.4.0 and the fix itself for fix versus v1.4.0. Thus the fixed code is present at the stated 1.4.0 boundary; the first-party advisory's `patched_versions: null` conflicts with its own resolution and repository tag ancestry, while its `< 1.4.0` boundary is consistent with v1.4.0 containing the fix.

AI attribution was taken only from `git cat-file -p 50bec5d3656d62b8dbbb0ce082fd67b8436677fd`: author and committer are Tobi <jahlives@gmx.ch>, and the commit message contains the exact Claude Code generation line and Claude Sonnet 4.5 Co-Authored-By trailer quoted in ai_marker. No later commit, fix authorship, branch name, or advisory text is used for attribution.
reasoning: The advisory's vulnerable unit is not a later refactor: it is the first AST visitor itself. The BIC created that visitor and made its allow-through result the gate before plugin import, while omitting checks for the dunder attributes needed for object-hierarchy and globals traversal. A -S history trace identifies that ordinary one-parent commit as the first and smallest writer, and the immediate parent has no analyzer path at all. The direct fix modifies precisely those visitor decisions by adding and enforcing a dangerous-dunder set, and repository ancestry places that fix in v1.4.0, matching the externally stated fixed boundary despite the first-party metadata's null patched_versions field. Because the causal BIC commit object explicitly says it was generated with Claude Code and co-authored by Claude Sonnet 4.5, the AI-attributed commit itself first wrote the flawed mechanism; this satisfies AI_ROOT_CAUSE rather than attribution based on the fix or later history.
